currentCoordinate.coordNote: The canonical marker follows the restored main fort and donjon ruin, not the complete historical fortress and forterrain.

previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The legacy point lay approximately 9.36 kilometres northeast of the documented Basmo main fort and had no identifiable source object.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The partially restored donjon and main-fort ruin on the steep hill between Rødenessjøen and Hemnessjøen, identified by OSM way 1263141701, Wikidata Q4867802 and Kulturminne ID 86068.
identity.identityProblem: Basmo was historically a larger fortified landscape with a donjon, retrenchment, batteries, outworks and approximately 40 buildings. The canonical point must identify the surviving main ruin without reducing the complete fortress landscape to one building centroid.
identity.splitReason: The visible main ruin is the strongest physical visitor anchor for the wider historical fortress. Additional military components remain associated context rather than independent canonical records in this production.

requiredEvidence: authoritative distinction between main fort and wider forterrain
official local history and restoration context
explicit rejection of the legacy point and broad locality substitutes

evidence.finding: The mapped fort building has centroid 59.61710, 11.53487 and represents the restored donjon and main ruin at Basmo.
evidence.reason: It directly identifies the surviving physical fort structure rather than a road, locality, bus stop or broad landscape point.

evidence.finding: The entity classifies Basmo as both fortress and cultural property, gives coordinate 59°37′0.8″N, 11°32′7.1″E and links Kulturminne ID 86068.
evidence.reason: Confirms the same fortress identity and places the entity within a few tens of metres of the applied main-ruin centroid.

evidence.finding: The national heritage identifier is linked to the Basmo fortress entity and its protected cultural-property status.
evidence.reason: Confirms the protected site identity while the mapped main-fort geometry supplies the applied coordinate.

evidence.finding: SNL places Basmo on a steep hill between Rødenessjøen and Hemnessjøen, distinguishes the small main-fort point from the approximate wider fortress and forterrain boundary, and describes the donjon, batteries, outworks and southern retrenchment.
evidence.reason: Defines the correct object role and prevents the main-ruin point or gameplay radius from being mistaken for the complete historical fortress.

evidence.finding: Marker municipality documents the five-storey, 18-metre tower completed in 1683, approximately 40 buildings, up to 1,350 men and 24 guns during the wars with Karl XII, closure in 1745, protection in 1985 and ongoing restoration.
evidence.reason: Confirms the main ruin's visitor identity and the much larger historical scale of the former military settlement.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 9,358.7 metres northeast of the named main-fort geometry.
evidence.reason: Replaced because it does not represent the Basmo fortress or its immediate landscape.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Entity and heritage cross-check; the mapped main-fort building geometry supplies the more direct physical anchor.
A broad locality or farm point does not identify the surviving fort ruin.
An access, road or parking point is visitor infrastructure rather than the historical object.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted main-ruin geometry, heritage identity, wider fortress scope, false-candidate controls and radius decision.

decision.nextAction: Applied the restored Basmo main-fort ruin centroid and retained the 320-metre gameplay radius. Continue with eidsberg_kirke.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 9.36 kilometres southwest.
The marker represents the restored main fort and donjon ruin as anchor for the wider historical fortress.
The complete forterrain, batteries, outworks and former settlement extend beyond the point and gameplay circle.
The radius is not a legal protection, property, building, ruin or complete fortress boundary.
